13.0.0.en: 1 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 2 Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel that prophesy, and say thou unto them that prophesy out of their own hearts, Hear ye the word of the LORD; 3 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Woe unto the foolish prophets, that follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing! 4 O Israel, thy prophets are like the foxes in the deserts. 5 Ye have not gone up into the gaps, neither made up the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the LORD. 6 They have seen vanity and lying divination, saying, The LORD saith: and the LORD hath not sent them: and they have made others to hope that they would confirm the word. 7 Have ye not seen a vain vision, and have ye not spoken a lying divination, whereas ye say, The LORD saith it; albeit I have not spoken? 8 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because ye have spoken vanity, and seen lies, therefore, behold, I am against you, saith the Lord GOD. 9 And mine hand shall be upon the prophets that see vanity, and that divine lies: they shall not be in the assembly of my people, neither shall they be written in the writing of the house of Israel, neither shall they enter into the land of Israel; and ye shall know that I am the Lord GOD. 10 Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace; and one built up a wall, and, lo, others daubed it with untempered morter: 11 Say unto them which daub it with untempered morter, that it shall fall: there shall be an overflowing shower; and ye, O great hailstones, shall fall; and a stormy wind shall rend it. 12 Lo, when the wall is fallen, shall it not be said unto you, Where is the daubing wherewith ye have daubed it? 13 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; I will even rend it with a stormy wind in my fury; and there shall be an overflowing shower in mine anger, and great hailstones in my fury to consume it. 14 So will I break down the wall that ye have daubed with untempered morter, and bring it down to the ground, so that the foundation thereof shall be discovered, and it shall fall, and ye shall be consumed in the midst thereof: and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 15 Thus will I accomplish my wrath upon the wall, and upon them that have daubed it with untempered morter, and will say unto you, The wall is no more, neither they that daubed it; 16 To wit, the prophets of Israel which prophesy concerning Jerusalem, and which see visions of peace for her, and there is no peace, saith the Lord GOD.

13.0.1.en: The Jews knew two kinds of false prophets: one kind represented idolatrous worship that openly resisted God, like the prophets of the groves whom the prophet Elijah killed (1 Kgs 18:40). The other kind prophesied out of the inspiration of their own hearts and feelings and private desires, in the name of God. Often they would say what pleased the heart of the king or the officials, out of their own invention, as a form of flattery (1 Kgs 22:5-28). This kind is more dangerous than the first, because they are deceivers who speak as those who carry divine inspiration while they carry the inspiration of their own evil selves. The prophet Jeremiah resists these, and so does Ezekiel.

13.1.0.en: He called them "fools, nebiem"; it is noted that the prophet plays on words, for instead of the word nebalim he says nebiem, just as in English one says profitless instead of prophets. The secret of their foolishness is that they prophesied "out of their own hearts" [2], they go "after their own spirit" [3] and not after the Spirit of the Lord, who is the Spirit of wisdom.

13.1.1.en: If God warns His people against the false prophets, He is at the same time concerned for these false ones to turn back from their evil and their lying, as Origen says: [There is no kind of sin that the Holy Scripture has not spoken of and made clear to its readers.

13.1.2.en: The word of God, sent to heal men, must deal with all kinds of sins and address all kinds of people, so that no one is deprived of the beneficial treatment or the useful medicine for healing his wound.

13.1.3.en: There are words that concern the people and others for the high priests, a third kind for the priests, and others for the shepherds and teachers. There are words that praise good teachers and words that rebuke the wicked, urging some to continue in goodness and others lest they sink into something worse than what they are in.

13.1.4.en: We need to interpret God's teachings about the false prophets... and to look at some of the teachers of the churches whose words or conduct do not agree with the doctrine they teach. They are false prophets.

13.1.5.en: We are very glad when we find the Holy Scripture urging us to keep away from vices, and we are even more glad when we find the word of God addressing and touching some orders of the Church, because we want healing from all sins.

13.1.6.en: "Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel" [2]. In Israel there were prophets in name and not in truth. And today there are also, in the true Israel, that is the Church, some false prophets and teachers, whom the word of God singles out with this prophecy. If the word of God concerns me, I must change my condition, by keeping away from vices, so that I may not be among those whom the Holy Scripture condemns here, but may become one of the teachers of the Church who spread the word of God with all faithfulness.

13.1.7.en: "Prophesy against the prophets of Israel that prophesy, and say thou unto them that prophesy out of their own hearts" [2-3]...

13.1.8.en: The word of God here refers to the teachers of the churches who speak what is contrary to the truth. To agree with the teachings of the Holy Spirit who spoke in the disciples is to speak not out of the (personal) heart but according to this Spirit who spoke in the Apostle Paul and the Apostle Peter and all the other disciples and apostles.

13.1.9.en: But if we read the Gospel and apply our own notions to it without truly understanding God's purposes, we become false prophets, speaking out of our own hearts in the Gospel.

13.1.10.en: As for the heretics... they expound their fables about the Aeons, relying on the Gospels and the Apostles, interpreting them out of their own hearts and not according to the Holy Spirit. They cannot say:

13.1.11.en: "For who hath known the mind of the Lord, that he may instruct him?

13.1.12.en: But we have the mind of Christ."

13.1.13.en: Or "Now we have received, not the spirit of the world, but the spirit which is of God; that we might know the things that are freely given to us of God" (1 Cor 2:12, 16)].

13.1.15.en: "They gather flocks against the house of Israel, who say:

13.2.0.en: In the day of the Lord they will not stand, they see vain visions" [5-6].

13.2.1.en: Origen comments on this phrase, saying: [They gather flocks that are separated from the Church of God and from the house of Israel.

13.2.2.en: They do not rise with the Lord Christ... because they see vain visions... they will not rise with Him, for those who truly rise say: "Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life" (Rom 6:4). For just as we have received "the earnest of the Spirit" (2 Cor 1:22), so we have received the earnest of the resurrection, since none of us has yet risen the complete resurrection...

13.2.3.en: They have not yet received the baptism of the resurrection, because they are false teachers and prophets... all that they see is vain; they cannot see the visions of truth... they have only false visions of the Holy Scripture].

13.2.4.en: "Therefore, behold, I am against you, saith the Lord GOD. And mine hand shall be upon the prophets that see vanity, and that divine lies" [8-9]. By human wisdom they wanted to win the people and to numb their consciences with false prophecy at the expense of the divine truth, so they lose the Lord, who becomes their adversary, and are removed from the people themselves: "They shall not be in the assembly of my people, neither shall they be written in the writing of the house of Israel, neither shall they enter into the land of Israel; and ye shall know that I am the Lord GOD. Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, Peace; and there was no peace" [9-10]. By their flattery of the people they wanted to utter soft words that they were in safety and peace, so they are deprived of the people, of the city and of the land!

13.3.0.en: St. Ambrose says: [You find in the Gospel a peace that Christ rejects, for He Himself says: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you" (Jn 14:27), for there is a peace that puts no stumbling block, and there is a peace that does. The one that puts no stumbling block is the peace of love, and the one that makes men stumble is the peace of appearances (hypocrisy). Therefore the prophet says: "Peace, peace; and there was no peace" [10].

13.3.1.en: Let us flee, then, from the peace of the wicked, for they conspire against the innocent, and gather together to oppress the righteous (Wis 2:12), and they overcome the widow and crush her humility].

13.3.2.en: They utter soft words... and as Origen says: [When the books are opened (Dan 7:10), by our words we are justified and by our words we are condemned (Mt 12:37), as the Lord Christ said. So the false teachers offer corrupt, destructive opinions that condemn them and do not justify them. And what happens with regard to words is likewise fulfilled with regard to deeds, for "some men's sins are open beforehand, going before to judgment; and some men they follow after. Likewise also the good works of some are manifest beforehand; and they that are otherwise cannot be hid" (1 Tim 5:24-25). Likewise, with regard to thoughts, they accuse or excuse (Rom 2:15). Let us then beware of our words, our deeds and our thoughts, lest they condemn us as false teachers!

13.3.3.en: St. Jerome says: [Those who came on their own account and were not sent are thieves and robbers (Jn 10:8)].

13.3.4.en: These false prophets became like foxes in the waste places [4], known for deceit; they ruin the city under the cover of "peace" instead of building it with good counsel. Instead of making up "the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the LORD" [5], that is, instead of building strong walls for its protection, behold, they daub the collapsing walls with untempered mortar [10], so that they have the appearance of strength, but only for a time, for the walls soon fall, because when the rains fall the real wall is exposed, and the mortar disappears and the stones of the wall are shown to be hailstones that the storms rend and shatter [11]. The deceptive layer of mortar that the false prophets set up disappears and the wall collapses completely:

13.3.5.en: "Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; I will even rend it with a stormy wind in my fury; and there shall be an overflowing shower in mine anger, and great hailstones in my fury to consume it. So will I break down the wall that ye have daubed with untempered morter, and bring it down to the ground, so that the foundation thereof shall be discovered, and it shall fall, and ye shall be consumed in the midst thereof: and ye shall know that I am the LORD" [13-14]. Thus the wrath of God falls on those who daubed it, and on the mortar they applied and on the wall itself.

13.4.0.en: It is noted that the prophet Ezekiel plays on words when he says: "Say unto them which daub it with untempered morter tapel, that it shall fall napel" [11].

13.5.0.en: This mortar is the soft, deceiving words: "Which see visions of peace for her, and there is no peace, saith the Lord GOD" [16]; and as it is written in Micah: "Thus saith the LORD concerning the prophets that make my people err, that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace" (Mic 3:5), and in Jeremiah: "For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace" (Jer 6:13-14).

13.5.1.en: Origen sees that the foxes [4] refer to the demons, as the psalmist says: "They shall go into the lower parts of the earth. They shall fall by the sword: they shall be a portion for foxes" (Ps 63:10-11). For foxes ruin the vines (Song 2:15)... It is as though these prophets, since they serve the kingdom of the devil, are counted as his soldiers or as evil spirits that spoil the vineyard of God.

13.5.2.en: Origen says: [We pass to another verse that rebukes these false prophets and teachers. And I ask to be kept from this rebuke by the power of your prayers for me.

13.5.4.en: "O Israel, thy prophets are like the foxes in the deserts" [4]. The fox is a useless animal, crafty, wild and predatory. The Savior says: "Tell that fox, Behold, I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected" (Lk 13:32).

13.5.5.en: Samson had need of these foxes against the strangers, for he caught 300 foxes and tied their tails together, and made them torches, and then let them go to burn the crops of the enemies (Judg 15:4-5). Such is the kind of the false teachers, for they are crafty and wicked, resembling these animals.

13.5.6.en: If I am like this, I am not only a fox but a fox in the waste places.

13.5.7.en: These hypocrites, crafty and worthless, dwell in the wilderness and the waste places, and are always in places isolated (from God). If God dwells in the soul, and it is filled with the Holy Spirit, the doctrines of the heretics cannot enter it. But if the Lord Christ is absent from it, then in these places the poisons of the wicked, erroneous teachings spread].

13.6.0.en: 17 Likewise, thou son of man, set thy face against the daughters of thy people, which prophesy out of their own heart; and prophesy thou against them, 18 And say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Woe to the women that sew pillows to all armholes, and make kerchiefs upon the head of every stature to hunt souls! Will ye hunt the souls of my people, and will ye save the souls alive that come unto you? 19 And will ye pollute me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, to slay the souls that should not die, and to save the souls alive that should not live, by your lying to my people that hear your lies? 20 Wherefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against your pillows, wherewith ye there hunt the souls to make them fly, and I will tear them from your arms, and will let the souls go, even the souls that ye hunt to make them fly. 21 Your kerchiefs also will I tear, and deliver my people out of your hand, and they shall be no more in your hand to be hunted; and ye shall know that I am the LORD. 22 Because with lies ye have made the heart of the righteous sad, whom I have not made sad; and strengthened the hands of the wicked, that he should not return from his wicked way, by promising him life: 23 Therefore ye shall see no more vanity, nor divine divinations: for I will deliver my people out of your hand: and ye shall know that I am the LORD.

13.7.0.en: The Holy Scripture mentions prophetesses to whom holy gifts were given, such as Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, who went out with a timbrel among the women singing the song of victory after the crossing of the Red Sea (Ex 15:20), and Deborah the judge (Judg 4:3-4), and the wife of Isaiah (Isa 8:3), and Huldah the prophetess (2 Kgs 22:14), and Anna the daughter of Phanuel (Lk 2:36), and the four daughters of Philip the evangelist (Acts 21:9). But here the prophet Ezekiel speaks of the false prophetesses who turned the word of the Lord into trade and material gain: "Will ye hunt the souls of my people, and will ye save the souls alive that come unto you? And will ye pollute me among my people for handfuls of barley and for pieces of bread, to slay the souls that should not die, and to save the souls alive that should not live, by your lying to my people that hear your lies?" [18-19]. It is a wicked trade; souls are sold at a paltry price, for a handful of barley or pieces of bread; they deliver innocent souls to death, and acquit wicked souls that deserve death.

13.7.1.en: They hunt human souls with soft words, gentle as pillows for every head, as though they were setting snares to catch birds. Therefore the Lord intervenes for the sake of His name, which these deceivers pollute, and for the sake of the poor souls that fall as their victims, so the Lord tears their pillows and delivers the people from their snares.

13.7.2.en: In the Septuagint it reads: "Woe to the women that sew pillows to hunt souls" [18]. These, as St. Ambrose says: [sew the old with the new... but our Christ has come, who made all things new (Rev 21:5), for He is the resurrection (Jn 11:25), the firstborn from the dead (Col 1:18); He does not leave us in our old man with its killing letter.

13.7.4.en: * You gave Your commandment to me as a priest, and You give it to the people also!

13.7.5.en: My soul is very precious in Your eyes, whether I am a master or a slave, old or young or a child, a man or a woman!

13.7.6.en: Your love is wondrous for every human soul, O my Lord!

13.7.7.en: * You warn me of the false prophets and the deceiving prophetesses, and at the same time You ask them to repent and return to You!

13.7.8.en: You hate deceit, yet You seek the souls of deceivers!

13.7.9.en: You hate heresies and innovations, yet You long for the repentance of heretics!

13.7.10.en: You are wondrous, O Savior of the world!

13.7.11.en: * Grant me not to fall into the deceit of soft words, nor to lean on the pillows of false teachers, nor to trust the sweetness of their tongue that is full of deadly poison!

13.7.12.en: * Keep me, lest my thoughts or my words or my deeds deceive me!

13.7.13.en: For I shall give account for every vain thought, and every idle word, and every work that is of no profit!
